title: Rigveda 10.78: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.78: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.78 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 44r-45r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.78.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 44r
translation.original_text:
1viprā̍so̱ na manma̍bhiḥ svā̱dhyo̍ devā̱vyo̱3̱̍ na ya̱jñaiḥ svapna̍saḥ | rājā̍no̱ na ci̱trāḥ su̍sa̱ṁdṛśa̍ḥ kṣitī̱nāṁ na maryā̍ are̱pasa̍ḥ ||
2a̱gnir na ye bhrāja̍sā ru̱kmava̍kṣaso̱ vātā̍so̱ na sva̱yuja̍ḥ sa̱dyaū̍tayaḥ | pra̱jñā̱tāro̱ na jyeṣṭhā̍ḥ sunī̱taya̍ḥ su̱śarmā̍ṇo̱ na somā̍ ṛ̱taṁ ya̱te ||
translation.text:
1Ye by your hymns are like high-thoughted singers, skilful, inviting Gods with sacrifices; Fair to behold, like Kings, with bright adornment, like spotless gallants, leaders of the people:
2Like fire with flashing flame, breast-bound with chains of gold, like tempest-blasts, self-moving, swift to lend your aid; As best of all foreknowers, excellent to guide, like Somas, good to guard the man who follows Law.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 44r (numbered 43r by the scribe) (OPenn image 43, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.77.7 ‹-devānām api gopīthe astu›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 44v (numbered 43v by the scribe), begins in RV 10.78.3 ‹-virokiṇaḥ›. Verses 10.78.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.78.3-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 44v
translation.original_text:
3vātā̍so̱ na ye dhuna̍yo jiga̱tnavo̍ 'gnī̱nāṁ na ji̱hvā vi̍ro̱kiṇa̍ḥ | varma̍ṇvanto̱ na yo̱dhāḥ śimī̍vantaḥ pitṝ̱ṇāṁ na śaṁsā̍ḥ surā̱taya̍ḥ ||
4rathā̍nā̱ṁ na ye1̱̍ 'rāḥ sanā̍bhayo jigī̱vāṁso̱ na śūrā̍ a̱bhidya̍vaḥ | va̱re̱yavo̱ na maryā̍ ghṛta̱pruṣo̍ 'bhisva̱rtāro̍ a̱rkaṁ na su̱ṣṭubha̍ḥ ||
5aśvā̍so̱ na ye jyeṣṭhā̍sa ā̱śavo̍ didhi̱ṣavo̱ na ra̱thya̍ḥ su̱dāna̍vaḥ | āpo̱ na ni̱mnair u̱dabhi̍r jiga̱tnavo̍ vi̱śvarū̍pā̱ aṅgi̍raso̱ na sāma̍bhiḥ ||
translation.text:
3Shakers of all, like gales of wind they travel, like tongues of burning fires in their effulgence. Mighty are they as warriors clad in armour, and, like the Fathers' prayers, Most Bounteous Givers.
4Like spokes of car-wheels in one nave united, ever victorious like heavenly Heroes, Shedding their precious balm like youthful suitors, they raise their voice and chant their psalm as singers.
5They who are fleet to travel like the noblest steeds, long to obtain the prize like bounteous charioteers, Like waters speeding on with their precipitous floods, like omniform Angirases with Sâma-hymns.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 44v (numbered 43v by the scribe) (OPenn image 44, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.78.3 ‹-virokiṇaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 45r (numbered 44r by the scribe), begins in RV 10.78.6 ‹-tviṣā›. Verses 10.78.3-5 end on this page; 10.78.3 begins on fol. 44r (numbered 43r by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.78.6-8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 3, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 45r
translation.original_text:
6grāvā̍ṇo̱ na sū̱raya̱ḥ sindhu̍mātara ādardi̱rāso̱ adra̍yo̱ na vi̱śvahā̍ | śi̱śūlā̱ na krī̱ḻaya̍ḥ sumā̱taro̍ mahāgrā̱mo na yāma̍nn u̱ta tvi̱ṣā ||
7u̱ṣasā̱ṁ na ke̱tavo̍ 'dhvara̱śriya̍ḥ śubha̱ṁyavo̱ nāñjibhi̱r vy a̍śvitan | sindha̍vo̱ na ya̱yiyo̱ bhrāja̍dṛṣṭayaḥ parā̱vato̱ na yoja̍nāni mamire ||
8su̱bhā̱gān no̍ devāḥ kṛṇutā su̱ratnā̍n a̱smān sto̱tṝn ma̍ruto vāvṛdhā̱nāḥ | adhi̍ sto̱trasya̍ sa̱khyasya̍ gāta sa̱nād dhi vo̍ ratna̱dheyā̍ni̱ santi̍ ||
translation.text:
6Born from the stream, like press-stones are the Princes, for ever like the stones that crush in pieces; Sons of a beauteous Dame, like playful children, like a great host upon the march with splendour.
7Like rays of Dawn, the visitors of sacrifice, they shine with ornaments as eager to be bright. Like rivers hasting on, glittering with their spears, from far away they measure out the distances.
8Gods, send us happiness and make us wealthy, letting us singers prosper, O ye Maruts. Bethink you of our praise and of our friendship: ye from of old have riches to vouchsafe us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 45r (numbered 44r by the scribe) (OPenn image 44, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.78.6 ‹-tviṣā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 45v (numbered 44v by the scribe), begins in RV 10.79.2 ‹sam bharanty uttānahastā namasādhi›. Verses 10.78.6-8 end on this page; 10.78.6 begins on fol. 44v (numbered 43v by the scribe).
